title: A clinical trial to learn more about the effects of remibrutinib in people with chronic pruritus (itch) of unknown origin
official: A 52-week multi-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo- controlled phase 3 study to evaluate the efficacy, safety and tolerability of remibrutinib in adult participants with severe chronic pruritus of unknown origin (CPUO)
summary: Main objective: To demonstrate that the efficacy of remibrutinib is superior to placebo in reducing pruritus severity in adult participants with severe CPUO after 12 weeks of treatment.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Participant must be ≥ 18 years of age, at the time of signing the informed consent.
2. Participants with chronic pruritus for at least 4 months prior to screening.
3. Chronic pruritus considered of unknown origin as assessed by the investigator at baseline (e.g., excluding chronic pruritus related to primary dermatological or systemic conditions, neuropathic or psychogenic origin or secondary to drugs or other allergen exposures). Dry skin (xerosis) will not be considered a primary cause for pruritus given the mandatory use of emollient throughout the study by all patients.
4. Chronic pruritus must affect at least 2 of the following body areas: trunk, arms, or legs (cannot be unilateral and/or dermatomal in distribution).
5. Participants with ongoing, severe chronic pruritus despite the use of emollients and who are candidates for systemic therapy.
6. Participants must have severe itch defined by a WI-NRS ≥7 at screening (completed in the participant’s eDiary dispensed at the screening visit for the duration of the study); score scale ranges from 0 to 10; higher score indicates worse itch.
7. Participants must have an average WI-NRS ≥7 over the 7 days prior to randomization/baseline visit (completed in the participant’s eDiary).
8. The average WI-NRS score over the preceding 7 days prior to the randomization/baseline visit will be calculated based on the daily WI-NRS scores (0- 10). Participants must have a minimum of 4 daily scores over this 7-day period to be considered eligible for randomization. If there is not a minimum of 4 daily scores available, the baseline/randomization visit can be postponed in order to have at least 4 daily scores over the preceding 7 days prior to randomization, but without exceeding the 28-day screening period.
9. Participants must have PGIS of pruritus scored as 3 "severe" at screening and baseline  visits.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Any active skin conditions (e.g., atopic dermatitis, psoriasis, etc.) that may interfere with the assessment of CPUO.
2. Known systemic condition(s) or medication(s) that are considered by the investigator to be the primary cause of current pruritus.
3. Use of other investigational drugs within 5 half-lives, or within 30 days (for small molecules), prior to randomization, or until the pharmacodynamic effect has returned to baseline (for biologics), whichever is longer. In these instances, the washout period can be extended as required by local regulations. Use of biologics investigated for the treatment of CPUO (including dupilumab, nemolizumab) 3 months prior to randomization until the end of the study.
4. Known or suspected infectious disease that is active, chronic or recurrent which precludes the participant from participating in the clinical trial as per Investigator´s assessment. These infectious diseases include but are not limited to opportunistic infections (e.g., tuberculosis, atypical mycobacterioses, listeriosis or aspergillosis) and/or known or suspected HIV infection.
5. History of malignancy of any organ system (other than localized basal cell carcinoma of the skin or in situ cervical cancer), treated or untreated, within the past 5 years, regardless of whether there is evidence of local recurrence or metastases.
6. Evidence of clinically significant cardiovascular (such as but not limited to myocardial infarction, unstable ischemic heart disease, New York Heart Association (NYHA) Class III/IV left ventricular failure, arrhythmia and uncontrolled hypertension within 12 months prior to Visit 1), neurological, psychiatric, pulmonary, renal, hepatic, endocrine, metabolic, hematological disorders, gastrointestinal disease or immunodeficiency that, in the Investigator's opinion, would compromise the safety of the participant, interfere with the interpretation of the study results or otherwise preclude participation or protocol adherence of the participant.
7. Significant bleeding risk or coagulation disorders. History of gastrointestinal bleeding, e.g., in association with use of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), that was clinically relevant (e.g., where intervention was indicated or requiring hospitalization or blood transfusion). Requirement for anti-platelet medication, except for acetylsalicylic acid up to 100 mg/d or clopidogrel up to 75 mg/d. The use of dual anti-platelet therapy (e.g., acetylsalicylic acid + clopidogrel) is prohibited.
8. History or current hepatic disease, including but not limited to, acute or chronic hepatitis, cirrhosis or hepatic failure or aspartate aminotransferase (AST)/ alanine aminotransferase (ALT) levels of more than 1.5 x upper limit of normal (ULN) or International Normalized Ratio (INR) of more than 1.5 at screening.
